given: A 640x480 image at <dir>/img.png. ExportContext.image_size is (h, w) = (480, 640) -- HEIGHT FIRST (exporters/__init__.py:102; the UI passes (pixmap.height(), pixmap.width()) at save_export_manager.py:397). The segment list holds exactly one segment with class_id 3, so class_order = get_unique_class_ids() = [3] (segment_manager.py:87-95) and that segment's channel index is 0 (segment_manager.py:276). YOLO_DETECTION is instance-aware (exporters/__init__.py:86-94), so ctx.instances is populated by create_instance_contours (save_export_manager.py:445-452, save_worker.py:92-98, main_window.py:6624-6630): the segment's own mask is ANDed with final_mask_tensor[:, :, 0] (segment_manager.py:297-299), i.e. AFTER crop zeroing (file_manager.py:712-739, applied at save_export_manager.py:412-417) and pixel priority (segment_manager.py:247-250). The pixels that survive form ONE 8-connected blob covering columns 100..109 and rows 50..59 inclusive. No crop is active.
when: export_all({ExportFormat.YOLO_DETECTION}, ctx) (exporters/__init__.py:189-206) invokes YoloDetectionExporter.export (yolo_detection.py:19-46). This is the ordinary save path: YOLO_DETECTION is one of the two DEFAULT_EXPORT_FORMATS (exporters/__init__.py:60-63).
then:
<dir>/img.txt -- os.path.splitext(image_path)[0] + '.txt' (yolo_detection.py:45-46) -- is created, or an existing file is truncated (open(path, 'w'), line 40), and its parent directory is created if missing (line 39). It receives exactly one line. cv2.boundingRect on that blob returns (x=100, y=50, bw=10, bh=10): the extent INCLUDES both edge pixels, so columns 100..109 give x=100 and bw=10, never 9 (yolo_detection.py:27; re-run against OpenCV 4.12.0). Then cx = (100 + 10/2)/640 = 0.1640625, cy = (50 + 10/2)/480 = 0.11458333333333333, nw = 10/640 = 0.015625, nh = 10/480 = 0.020833333333333332 (yolo_detection.py:29-32). The file content is exactly these bytes -- five fields separated by single ASCII spaces, class token first, no rounding, no truncation, no fixed decimal count, followed by one line terminator (yolo_detection.py:33, 41-42):
3 0.1640625 0.11458333333333333 0.015625 0.020833333333333332<LF>
The card's '0.114583...' and '0.020833...' are the truncated forms and must never be emitted: the exact digit strings above are the contract. The terminator is CR LF (0x0D 0x0A) when the legacy app runs on Windows, because line 40 opens the file in Python text mode with newline=None (verified: the byte stream is b'3 0.5 0.5 1.0 1.0\r\n'); it is LF alone on Linux/macOS.
and: AND (1) GRANULARITY -- one line per OUTER CONTOUR, not per object. iter_object_contours yields every contour of every instance record (exporters/__init__.py:122-126) and create_instance_contours runs cv2.findContours(single, RETR_EXTERNAL, CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) separately per segment (segment_manager.py:303-305). One segment whose surviving pixels fall into two islands therefore writes TWO lines with two separate boxes, never one box around both (verified: islands at rows 10-19/cols 10-19 and rows 100-119/cols 300-339 produced rects (300,100,40,20) and (10,10,10,10), i.e. two lines). Holes are dropped (RETR_EXTERNAL). The docstring phrase 'One line per object' (yolo_detection.py:16) is wrong and must not be copied into the TS implementation. AND (2) LINE ORDER -- lines follow ctx.instances order, which is segment-list order (segment_manager.py:279), and within one segment OpenCV's contour order, which is NOT top-to-bottom: in the verified two-island case the LOWER island (y=100) was emitted first. Lines are never sorted by class id in this path. AND (3) FALLBACK PATH -- when ctx.instances is empty (falsy, so an empty list counts) the exporter instead contours the merged per-class channels of mask_tensor (exporters/__init__.py:128-136). That path emits lines in ascending channel index = ascending class id (class_order is sorted), skips all-zero channels, and FUSES touching or overlapping same-class objects into a single box. AND (4) NUMBER FORMAT -- the four coordinates are Python float repr, not 'full precision' in any looser sense; see parameters for the exact rule and the TS function that reproduces it. The two places a naive JavaScript writer diverges are whole numbers (Python '1.0' vs JS '1') and values below 1e-4 (Python '6.103515625e-05' vs JS '0.00006103515625'). AND (5) EVERY line, including the last, ends with a terminator (yolo_detection.py:42); the file never ends without one and never has a blank last line beyond that terminator. AND (6) CLASS TOKEN -- the decimal integer class_order[channel] (yolo_detection.py:28), i.e. the original class id, never the 0..N-1 channel index and never the alias/label string. AND (7) WRITING NEVER DELETES -- export_all only writes (exporters/__init__.py:189-206, docstring at 190-197); other formats' files sitting beside the image are left untouched.
edgeCases: h <= 0 or w <= 0: nothing is written and export returns None (yolo_detection.py:21-22). Note the single-view UI never reaches this guard -- _build_export_context raises ValueError('No image loaded (pixmap is empty)') first (save_export_manager.py:398-399) -- so it is reachable only via the worker/multi-view paths or a directly constructed ExportContext.

No contours at all (every channel empty, or every segment's pixels removed by crop/pixel priority): export returns None WITHOUT writing and WITHOUT deleting, so a stale <base>.txt from an earlier save survives with outdated boxes (yolo_detection.py:35-36; pinned by test_bbox_roundtrip.py:438-452). Outputs are deleted only when the image has no segments at all, and then for every format at once (save_export_manager.py:106-109 -> 523-529 -> exporters/__init__.py:209-215).

ctx.instances empty triggers the merged-channel fallback (exporters/__init__.py:122 tests truthiness). This is not only the no-instance-data case: if every segment is skipped by create_instance_contours -- mask is None or mask.shape[:2] != image_size (segment_manager.py:294-295), or the AND with the final tensor leaves nothing (segment_manager.py:300-301) -- the list comes back empty and the exporter silently switches to contouring the merged channels, changing both line order (ascending class id) and granularity (touching same-class objects fuse).

A segment made of two disconnected blobs produces two lines, each with its own box; the lower blob came first in the verified case, so line order must not be assumed top-to-bottom (segment_manager.py:303-305, exporters/__init__.py:122-126).

Crop does not change the coordinate frame: crop zeroes pixels outside the rectangle (file_manager.py:712-739) but image_size stays the FULL image (save_export_manager.py:397, 412-421), so coordinates are still divided by full width/height and are not shifted to the crop origin. A crop can shrink a box, or split one segment into several lines.
Pixel priority (segment_manager.py:247-250) can likewise shrink or split a box, because each segment's mask is ANDed with the post-priority channel (segment_manager.py:297-299).

Non-contiguous class ids are written as-is: class_order=[3,7] writes tokens '3' and '7' (yolo_detection.py:28; pinned by tests/unit/core/exporters/test_exporters.py:301-320 and test_bbox_roundtrip.py:513-523).
A box spanning the full width or height writes nw/nh as '1.0' (Python), where JS String() would write '1'. cx and cy can never be exactly 0.0 or 1.0 because bw, bh >= 1.

Any coordinate below 1e-4 is written in Python scientific notation with a two-digit exponent, e.g. a 1x1 px box at (0,0) of an 8192x8192 image writes '0 6.103515625e-05 6.103515625e-05 0.0001220703125 0.0001220703125'. JS String() would write '0.00006103515625' for the first two fields.
Line terminator is platform-dependent in the legacy writer (text mode, yolo_detection.py:40): CRLF on Windows, LF on Linux/macOS. Every line ends with one, including the last.

DO NOT port FileManager.save_bb_txt (file_manager.py:74-123). It writes to the same <base>.txt path but emits class_labels[channel] -- the alias NAME, e.g. 'dog' -- instead of the id (line 105), always uses the merged-channel path (lines 96-103), and calls os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_path)) without the `or '.'` fallback (line 118), which raises FileNotFoundError for a bare relative filename. Nothing in the app calls it; only tests do.

The loader reads this file back last in the priority chain (exporters/__init__.py:73-81; file_manager._LOAD_CHAIN:128-136) via load_bb_txt (file_manager.py:412-454): lines with other than 5 whitespace-separated fields or unparseable floats are skipped (lines 432-440), and corners are recovered as int(round((cx -/+ bw/2) * w)) (lines 446-449), i.e. the reload is round-trip-exact for integer pixel boxes but is not the inverse of boundingRect's inclusive convention in general.
answer: No -- YOLO class indices must NOT be renumbered to a contiguous 0..N-1 range, and a TS port that does so is a data-corruption bug. The legacy writer emits class_order[channel] (yolo_detection.py:28), where class_order is the sorted unique class ids present in that ONE image (segment_manager.py:87-95) and channel is merely the position in that list (segment_manager.py:221, 276); the contiguous 0..N-1 value exists only as the channel index and is never written. That matches the approved decisions (keep legacy per-image class ids and aliases; exports byte-identical to legacy): ids are per-image, therefore sparse and not dataset-global -- the same dataset can legitimately contain img_a.txt with tokens 3 and 7 and img_b.txt with token 0 -- and the app reloads the token as an int or as an existing alias name (file_manager.py:345-376, 436), so renumbering would break the app's own reload; two tests pin it (tests/unit/core/exporters/test_exporters.py:301-320, test_bbox_roundtrip.py:513-523). What the card got wrong: (1) 'One line per object' -- the code writes one line per OUTER CONTOUR; iter_object_contours yields every contour of every instance record (exporters/__init__.py:122-126) and create_instance_contours calls findContours with RETR_EXTERNAL per segment (segment_manager.py:303-305), so a segment split into two islands writes two lines (I reproduced this: rects (300,100,40,20) and (10,10,10,10)). The phrase survives only in a docstring (yolo_detection.py:16) and must not be ported. (2) The 'then' line was truncated ('0.114583...', '0.020833...'); the contract strings are '3 0.1640625 0.11458333333333333 0.015625 0.020833333333333332', which I re-derived by running the exporter's arithmetic against OpenCV 4.12.0 (yolo_detection.py:27-33). (3) 'floats written unrounded (full precision)' is too vague to implement: the f-string at yolo_detection.py:33 is Python float repr, which appends '.0' to whole numbers and switches to two-digit-exponent scientific notation below 1e-4, where JavaScript's String() writes '1' and '0.00006103515625'. Over 8013 values generated from real (x+bw/2)/w and bw/w computations, String(v) differed from Python on 421; the pyRepr function given in parameters matched all 8013. (4) The card stated no line order, no line terminator and no overwrite semantics: order is segment-list order then OpenCV contour order (lower island first in my test), never sorted by class in the instance path, while the fallback path (exporters/__init__.py:128-136) orders by ascending class id and fuses touching same-class objects; every line ends with a terminator that Python text mode writes as CRLF on Windows (yolo_detection.py:40-42, verified byte-for-byte); open(...,'w') truncates and line 39 creates the parent directory. (5) The guard is h <= 0 or w <= 0, not just 0 (yolo_detection.py:21-22), and the single-view UI raises before that guard is ever reached (save_export_manager.py:398-399). Two further traps for the implementer: ctx.instances being an EMPTY list silently selects the merged-channel fallback (exporters/__init__.py:122), which can happen in production when a segment's mask shape does not match image_size (segment_manager.py:294-295); and FileManager.save_bb_txt (file_manager.py:74-123) is a dead second writer for the same .txt path that emits the alias NAME instead of the class id (line 105) -- do not use it as the reference implementation.

unresolved: Two items need the product owner. (1) Line endings: 'byte-identical to legacy output' is ambiguous because the legacy bytes are platform-dependent -- Python text mode (yolo_detection.py:40) writes CRLF on Windows and LF on Linux/macOS. The TS writer must be told whether to mirror the host OS (matching whichever machine the legacy app ran on) or to pin one terminator; golden files captured on Windows will fail an LF writer and vice versa. (2) Byte-identity implies reproducing OpenCV's cv2.findContours (Suzuki-Abe, RETR_EXTERNAL, CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) contour ENUMERATION ORDER, not just the boxes, because line order is observable in the file. The PO should decide whether the TS stack takes an OpenCV binding/WASM build or accepts a hand-ported tracer whose ordering must then be characterised against the legacy output.
